newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal peace talks end without deal.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal peace talks end without deal.

text.p: Government and rebel leaders ended three days of talks in Dhaka on Monday without reaching a deal to halt the revolt in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts, but said they would meet again.
Negotiators on both sides said significant progress had been made.
"During the three days, we have reached a consensus on a number of issues," the government's chief negotiator, Abul Hasanat Abdullah, told reporters.
"We will meet again on March 12," he said before the rebel leaders left the State Guest House to board a military helicopter on their way to Dudukchhari, a Hill Tracts village near the Indian boder.

The talks began on Saturday after five leaders of the rebel Shanti Bahini, led by Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, flew to the city for their first peace meeting with the government outside the hill region.

Both Abdullah, a parliamentary member from the ruling Awami League, and Larma, chief of the Shanti Bahini's political wing, gave no details of the issues on which they reached consensus or those that barred them from signing a deal.
"These cannot be disclosed in the interest of the next round (of talks)," Larma said.
The Shanti Bahini has fought a bush war since 1973 for autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, which border India and Burma.
The rebels also want 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.

Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has forced around 50,000 tribespeople to seek refuge in the northeastern Indian state of Tripura.
Abdullah said the venue of the next meeting would be decided later.
